question: Where is the cervix located in the female reproductive system?

options.A: The muscular upper walls of the uterine cavity
options.B: The lower portion of the uterus opening into the vagina
options.C: The tube connecting the ovary to the main uterus
options.D: The inner lining where a fertilized egg implants

explanation: The cervix is the lower, narrow neck of the uterus that links the main uterine cavity to the vaginal canal. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why is the transformation zone of the cervix clinically important?

options.A: It is where most cervical cancer precursors originate
options.B: It regulates the monthly shedding of the endometrium
options.C: It produces the thick mucus plug during pregnancy
options.D: It prevents bacterial entry into the upper reproductive tract

explanation: The transformation zone undergoes constant cell changes, making it the primary site where abnormal cell growth starts. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h1)

question: Which high-risk types of human papillomavirus (HPV) cause most cervical cancers?
explanation: HPV strains 16 and 18 are the main high-risk types linked to the majority of invasive cervical cancers worldwide. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h2)

question: How does an HIV co-infection increase the risk of cervical cancer?

options.A: It impairs the immune system from clearing persistent HPV infections
options.B: It causes immediate physical trauma to the cervical mucosa
options.C: It directly mutates the squamous cells in the transformation zone
options.D: It accelerates the production of estrogen in the ovaries

explanation: A weakened immune system struggles to fight off and clear ongoing high-risk HPV infections. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is the function of the viral E6 and E7 proteins in HPV infections?

options.A: They stimulate rapid antibody production to trick the immune system
options.B: They destroy local blood vessels to starve healthy tissues
options.C: They inactivate host tumor suppressor proteins like p53 and Rb
options.D: They form a protective outer capsule shielding the virus

explanation: Proteins E6 and E7 interfere with normal cell cycle control by blocking crucial tumor suppressor mechanisms. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h3)

question: At which stage are abnormal cells confined to the tissue layer without breaking through the basement membrane?
explanation: Carcinoma in situ means severe cell changes affect the full epithelial layer, but the basement membrane remains unbroken. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is usually the first noticeable symptom of developing cervical cancer?
explanation: Bleeding between periods or after sexual intercourse is a common early warning sign of cervical cell disruption. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h4)

question: A patient presents with lower leg swelling and severe pelvic pain radiating down the flank. What does this suggest?

options.A: A benign inflammatory polyp in the upper vaginal canal
options.B: An early localized infection confined to the transformation zone
options.C: Advanced tumor growth pressing on pelvic walls and lymphatics
options.D: Normal physiological changes related to hormonal fluctuations

explanation: When a tumor spreads to the pelvic wall and blocks lymphatic vessels, it causes radiating pain and swelling in the legs. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h4)

question: Which solution is applied to the cervix during Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA)?
explanation: Acetic acid is essentially dilute vinegar, which makes abnormal, protein-dense cells turn white temporarily for easy viewing. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h5)

question: Why is Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid helpful in low-resource community health settings?

options.A: It provides definitive histological confirmation of invasive cancer
options.B: It provides immediate results without requiring a pathology laboratory
options.C: It completely replaces the need for any future HPV vaccination
options.D: It eliminates all false-positive readings associated with normal tissue

explanation: VIA lets healthcare workers see abnormal patches right away, enabling quick discussions and same-day treatment in remote areas. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h5)

question: What instrument is used during a colposcopy to get a magnified view of the cervix?
explanation: A colposcope is an illuminated magnification tool that helps providers examine the cervix closely for unusual blood vessel patterns. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a cervical biopsy after an abnormal screening test?

options.A: To prevent future transmission of sexually transmitted infections
options.B: To measure the exact circulating viral load in the bloodstream
options.C: To obtain tissue samples for definitive histological examination
options.D: To destroy all remaining dysplastic cells in the transformation zone

explanation: Looking at a small tissue sample under a microscope confirms whether precancerous changes or cancer are actually present. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h6)

question: Which surgical procedure removes the cervix while trying to preserve fertility in young patients with early-stage disease?
explanation: A radical trachelectomy removes the cervix and upper vagina but leaves the main body of the uterus intact for future pregnancies. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h7)

question: Why are chemotherapy and radiation therapy sometimes combined in cervical cancer treatment?

options.A: To permanently eliminate dormant high-risk viral particles from skin
options.B: To stimulate rapid regeneration of normal squamous epithelial cells
options.C: To replace the need for any subsequent surgical tumor removal
options.D: To radiosensitize cancer cells and make them more vulnerable to radiation

explanation: Certain chemotherapy drugs make cancer cells more sensitive, helping radiation destroy the tumor cells more effectively. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h7)

question: What is an important nursing care focus for a patient undergoing pelvic radiation therapy?

options.A: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics to prevent viral shedding
options.B: Monitoring for signs of radiation cystitis and bowel irritation
options.C: Applying harsh antiseptic ointments directly to the external os
options.D: Encouraging immediate high-impact exercises to boost immunity

explanation: Pelvic radiation can affect nearby organs like the bladder and bowels, so nurses must watch closely for signs of inflammation. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h8)

question: A patient with advanced cervical cancer reports severe pelvic pain that interrupts sleep. What is the priority nursing action?

options.A: Reassuring the patient that pelvic pain is a normal expected recovery sign
options.B: Instructing the patient to restrict fluid intake to reduce pelvic pressure
options.C: Advising immediate discontinuation of all prescribed chemotherapeutic drugs
options.D: Collaborating with the care team to implement structured pain management

explanation: Palliative care focuses heavily on assessing pain accurately and giving timely medications to keep the patient comfortable. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h8)

question: When is the HPV vaccine most effective at preventing cervical cancer?

options.A: Immediately following a positive Pap smear
options.C: After the diagnosis of stage one dysplasia
options.D: Before the onset of sexual activity

explanation: The vaccine works best when given before a person is first exposed to high-risk HPV strains through sexual contact. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h9)

question: Why do barrier methods like condoms fail to provide total protection against HPV?

options.A: HPV is primarily transmitted through airborne respiratory droplets
options.B: The virus can infect surrounding skin areas not covered by the condom
options.C: Latex material is structurally permeable to active viral particles
options.D: Spermicidal lubricants chemically neutralize the protective vaccine

explanation: HPV spreads via skin-to-skin contact in the genital region, leaving areas outside the barrier exposed to the virus. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h9)
